chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Razin, the master of the Anmat, from one of the two (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever says: 'O Allah, I call You to witness, and I call Your亲近 angels and the chosen bearers of Your Throne to witness that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the Beneficent, the Merciful; and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger; and that So-and-so and So-and-so are my Imam and my Guardian; and that their father is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, and So-and-so and So-and-so, until it reaches him (Al-Qaim), [these] are my Imams and my Guardians. Upon this I live, and upon this I die, and upon this I will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment; and I disavow So-and-so and So-and-so and So-and-so.' If he dies on that night, he will enter Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for morning and evening that guarantees Paradise if one dies on that night?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the 'Tasbih of the Imams,' a comprehensive declaration of faith that integrates Tawhid, Nabuwwah, and specifically Imamah by naming the Twelve Imams as spiritual authorities. In Shia tradition, this practice underscores the necessity of recognizing the divine appointment of the Imams, with the promise of Paradise for those who die upon this specific creed. It serves as a daily ritual reinforcing the believer's allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt and their disavowal of opposing factions.
